items.title: 68436_Alberta Hunter oral history interview
items.q: He wrote me a letter first and I answered his letter... I mentioned something to him about 'Downhearted Blues'. That's how 'Downhearted Blues' happened to be mentioned in his letter.

ctx.x: Into the tape. It's from the Columbia Graphophone Company, 1819 Broadway, New York City, recording studios, dated January 19th, 1923, addressed to Miss Alberta Hunter, number 64 East 36th Place, Chicago, Illinois. "Dear Miss Hunter. Replying to your letter of the 15th instant, won't you please advise me at your earliest convenience just how long your exclusive contract with the Paramount Company runs. No doubt you know that the Paramount Company is very small indeed, and the prestige that you gain from singing…
Now, you had apparently written them a letter about "Downhearted Blues".
